No test was visible in this file.
The cache is kept per server process, so each server builds its own copy.

terms.meaning: Showing a saved result again without re-running the work that produced it.
A fixed choice of saved run that does not change automatically.
A stored copy kept so it can be reused instead of rebuilt.
A full, independent duplicate of data, so changes to the copy do not touch the original.

sections.name: File setup, Validation, QA
sections.title: Imports, types and header rules
sections.what: Loads the saved run data, deck readers, helpers and the pin check, and defines the shape of evidence examples and questions. The header rules state that the replay is read only.
sections.why: The header records the design goal: demos should be safe to repeat.
sections.watch_out: The read-only promise holds only while no helper here writes data. A later edit could break it.

sections.name: DemoHint, n, short, day
sections.title: Hint shape and small text helpers
sections.what: Defines a short hint note that points to a control, slide or tab and can open a citation. Also defines helpers for number formatting, shortening names and showing dates.
sections.why: Hints keep the walkthrough consistent. Reason beyond that not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Dates are shown in UTC, so a date near midnight may appear one day off for some viewers.

sections.name: sourceRef
sections.title: Turning a passage into a source reference
sections.what: Converts a checked evidence passage into the source format used by citations, including its publisher and capture date.
sections.why: Citations elsewhere expect one common format.
sections.watch_out: A missing publisher is left blank, so the citation may show less detail.

sections.name: stageRows
sections.title: Turning stage records into rows
sections.what: Sorts stage records by start time and turns each into a labelled row with status, times and a detail sentence.
sections.why: The demo shows each stage of the saved run in its original order.
sections.watch_out: The sort changes the order of the array it is given, which can surprise other code that uses that array.

sections.name: requirePin
sections.title: Refusing a failed pin
sections.what: Stops the demo with a conflict error that lists the reasons the pin check failed.
sections.why: The demo must not present a saved run that no longer matches the data.
sections.watch_out: The reasons text is shown to the user, so it must stay readable.

sections.name: pickExample
sections.title: Choosing the example passage
sections.what: Picks the first evidence passage in preference order: Gorgon, then Wheatstone, then Ichthys projects, with budget passages before others.
sections.why: The comment says budget passages come first, and that the Gorgon date quote describes the actual date. Likely reason: budget figures are what the demo needs to show.
sections.watch_out: Project names are hardcoded, so a renamed project silently drops out of the preference order.

sections.name: buildScan (part 1)
sections.title: Building the Reality Scan walkthrough, first half
sections.what: Loads the pinned scan run, its deck copy and evidence passages, chooses an example project, and writes the research answer, questions and coverage figures for the cost and capacity charts.
sections.why: The walkthrough explains why only some projects appear on the charts.
sections.watch_out: If no example evidence exists, a conflict error is thrown. A bad source address throws while citations are built.

sections.name: buildScan (part 2)
sections.title: Building the Reality Scan walkthrough, second half
sections.what: Writes the hints, the assistant answer and a proposed chart title amendment, then returns the full scan presentation.
sections.why: The amendment shows a suggested title change the user can accept or dismiss.
sections.watch_out: The chart title element is assumed to exist, so a change to the deck could crash this step.

sections.name: buildLessons, Prepared, ready (part 1)
sections.title: Building the Lessons Learnt walkthrough, first half
sections.what: Loads the pinned lessons run, its saved result, deck and stages, picks an example passage from its factbase, lists featured cautionary cases, counts Australian cases and writes the summary questions.
sections.why: The walkthrough shows what the run found and how its projects turned out.
sections.watch_out: Cost overrun percentages come from the stored data and are only rounded for display.

sections.name: buildLessons, Prepared, ready (part 2)
sections.title: Building the Lessons Learnt walkthrough, second half
sections.what: Writes the hints, an assistant answer that explains how to check the example quote, and the executive title amendment, then returns the lessons presentation.
sections.why: Gives the user a way to verify the example quote on their own.
sections.watch_out: A conflict error is thrown if the executive summary title is missing.

sections.name: preparedDemo
sections.title: Caching the prepared walkthroughs
sections.what: Returns a stored walkthrough for each tool for up to ten minutes, rebuilds it when it expires, and gives each caller an independent copy.
sections.why: Building a walkthrough reads many records, so caching avoids repeating that work. The copy keeps edits from changing the cache.
sections.watch_out: A failed build is removed from the cache, but a successful one can serve old data for up to ten minutes after the pinned data changes.

summary: Builds the read-only walkthrough data for the pinned Reality Scan and Lessons Learnt runs, and keeps it in memory for ten minutes.
purpose: Gives the guided demos their questions, hints, evidence examples, amendments and slide deck, all taken from saved results.
why: The header says the replay makes no research or model requests, creates no runs, and writes nothing to saved decks or project data. Likely reason for the cache: avoid rebuilding the walkthrough on every request.
how: The file checks the pin for the chosen tool, loads the saved run, finds a verified evidence passage, and assembles questions, hints, a proposed title amendment and the deck. Results are kept for ten minutes and each caller receives an independent copy.
inputs: The tool name, scan or lessons. It reads saved runs, stage results, decks, evidence examples and the pin check.
outputs: A presentation object containing the deck, questions, hints, amendment, verification totals, coverage, stages and a pin record.
risks: Several branches throw conflict errors when required evidence is missing. The cache lasts ten minutes, so a change to pinned data can show old content until it expires. A malformed source address would throw while citations are built.
debug: A conflict error names the pin problem or the missing evidence; run the pin check first. If content looks stale, wait for the cache to expire or restart the server. The error text names the provisioning script to run for missing evidence.
